transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Sarah Blake (Oakridge - Head of Cloud Ops), Tom Nguyen (Oakridge - CISO), Priya Kapoor (Oakridge - Legal/Compliance)

Summary: quick discovery re: data residency and compliance requirements for Oakridge Bank. Primary concern: bank needs EU and US data residency separations, strict logging retention/obfuscation rules for PII, SOC2/HIPAA-like controls for certain workloads, and desire to evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options. Next steps agreed: security docs, VPC/on-prem design, schedule benching deep-dive.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — I'm Maya, account exec at Redwood, and Liam is our solutions engineer.
[00:06] Sarah: Hi all — Sarah here. We're trying to figure out options for hosting inference for a small set of customer-facing assistants. very sensitive stuff, banking PII.
[00:12] Tom: Tom Nguyen, CISO — I'll be focused on controls, encryption, and auditability.
[00:16] Priya: Priya, legal and compliance — interested in retention policies and any logging that could include personal data.
[00:21] Liam: Thanks. quick note on agenda: understand current stack, residency requirements, compliance gates (SOC2/HIPAA/GDPR), and then walk through hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs.

[03:05] Maya: Sarah, can you describe your current infra? where do you run other ML services?
[03:12] Sarah: Mainly AWS us-east for customer facing stuff, but we've got EU customers and some data categorization rules. our policy right now says EU customer data must remain in eu regions and cannot be exported. we also have a small on-prem datacenter for legacy systems.
[03:30] Liam: ok that makes sense. Oakridge' typical flow — requests hit your API, you decide if it includes PII, and then potentially send to model. do you currently mask or tokenize prior to sending out?
[03:42] Sarah: on some flows yes, others no. the problem is staff want features so sometimes PII slips through. hence compliance is strict.

[06:10] Tom: high level question: does Redwood hosted keep logs with raw prompts? we can't allow raw customer PII to be stored long-term outside our control.
[06:18] Maya: good question. Redwood Hosted by default stores request/response logs for troubleshooting and billing, but we have policies and retention settings and enterprise options. for regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private — Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in our infra with stricter retention and isolated pools; Private gives you a customer-controlled plane in VPC or on-prem where logs never leave your environment.
[06:45] Priya: and what about encryption and key management? we need KMS/HSM integration, ability to rotate keys, and ideally customer-managed keys.
[06:53] Liam: yes — we support CMEK for Dedicated and Private, integration with AWS KMS and external HSMs via the private deployment. Hosted can also use tenant keys for certain plans but there's a difference in guarantees.
[07:12] Sarah: GDPR is also a concern — data residency for EU subjects. can Redwood pin data to eu-west?
[07:18] Maya: yes. region pinning is supported. Hosted can scope to a region but again retention/logging controls are stronger on Dedicated/Private. there's also automatic data purging options and PII redaction tooling we can layer in.

[09:40] Sarah: ok, cost is a factor. what's the delta between hosted and dedicated for a bank our size? we expect sustained traffic but not huge.
[09:48] Maya: rough ballpark: Hosted is pay-as-you-go per-token, lower entry cost. Dedicated is monthly reserved capacity — higher committed cost but unit token price much lower and you get isolation. Private (VPC) tends to have a platform fee plus infra costs. i'll send a tailored pricing example after we get estimated qps.

[12:05] Tom: audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for every request and who accessed models. How does Redwood handle audit logging and RBAC?
[12:12] Liam: we provide audit logs with timestamps, request IDs, and user ids. for Dedicated/Private you can route logs to your SIEM (eg. Splunk) and keep longer retention. RBAC with SSO/SAML is supported — you can map roles and get admin vs ops vs viewer levels.
[12:34] Priya: retention policies — we need to guarantee deletion of logs containing PII after X days and have proofs for auditors. can you provide attestation?
[12:43] Maya: yes we can provide SOC2 attestation and a data processing addendum (DPA) for GDPR. for Dedicated/Private we can do contractual terms to meet retention windows. we'll share the SOC2 and ISO docs in the pack.

[15:20] Sarah: technical detail: we have a use-case where model prompts include account numbers in the first 100 tokens, then rest is context. we need prefix caching and low latency but also cannot store raw prompts. any ideas?
[15:32] Liam: two patterns — redact/tokenize at proxy layer before sending; or use Dedicated with in-flight KV caching disabled and have ephemeral caching only in RAM with no persistent logs. Redwood runtime supports KV cache management and you can tune caching and batching. for strict PII flows we recommend redaction + dedicated so you get performance but no logs persisted.

[18:00] Tom: for HIPAA — some of our BSA/AML teams work with health-adjacent info occasionally; is Redwood comfortable with HIPAA-level controls?
[18:08] Maya: Redwood can meet HIPAA requirements under dedicated/private setups, with BAAs for qualifying customers. Hosted is more limited unless under specific enterprise agreements.

[20:25] Priya: on legal — can logs be segregated per customer and exported on request for subject access requests?
[20:33] Liam: yes, per-tenant logs and we support data export endpoints. for subject access requests you can pull logs and delete entries per retention policy; in Private deployment those logs live in your infra so it's straightforward.

[23:10] Sarah: network controls — we need VPC peering, enforced egress rules, and allowlist IPs. can we have a private endpoint?
[23:18] Liam: Dedicated supports private endpoints and VPC peering; Private deployment is fully in your VPC with private endpoints only. we'll share network diagrams.

[26:45] Maya: competitors — asked earlier, who else are you evaluating?
[26:51] Tom: Anthropic and OpenAI for hosted, and our infra team is also evaluating self-hosting options for total control. latency/cost tradeoff is huge.
[27:05] Maya: noted. on benchmarking, if you want to test dedicated we can provision a reserved node for a pilot and run latency tests.

[29:12] Sarah: callbacks and retraining — do you keep training data? we will never allow PII to be used for model training.
[29:20] Liam: we do not use customer data for model training unless explicitly opted-in per DPA. we'll include that in the contract language.

[32:00] Tom: logging restrictions: can we mask tokens at ingestion automatically? we'd prefer server-side token masking so developers don't need to do it everywhere.
[32:09] Liam: we have middleware examples that do PII detection and masking; it's not perfect but can catch common patterns. we also recommend pre-send redaction at app layer as defense-in-depth.

[34:40] Priya: legal — data processing agreement and standard contractual clauses for EU transfers?
[34:47] Maya: yes, SCCs available and DPA will be included. for Private deployments transfers are not needed since data stays in your region.

[36:50] Sarah: we need to know what logs look like — schema, fields, and whether full prompt is stored.
[36:58] Liam: we'll attach sample log schema in the security pack; highlights: request_id, timestamp, model, tokens_count, user_id, and an optional field for redacted_prompt. full_prompt can be stored only if you enable debug logging; default is redacted or truncated in enterprise configs.

[39:20] Maya: to recap, Oakridge needs EU pinning, customer-managed keys, strict retention and redaction, SIEM export, and either Dedicated or Private preferred. next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO pack + log schema, Liam will send VPC/on-prem diagram, and we schedule a technical deep dive with Tom and infra next week.
[39:40] Tom: sounds good. also please include estimated committed monthly cost for a small dedicated footprint so we can compare.
[39:48] Maya: will do — i'll include a sample price sheet.

[41:00] Priya: one more — any third-party subprocessors? we need a list.
[41:07] Maya: yes we'll include subprocessors list in the security pack and the DPA.

[43:10] Sarah: ok thanks everyone, we'll review the docs and pick a time for the deep-dive.
[43:18] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with the items we discussed.

(Transcript ends)

References shared during call: Security pack link (placeholder): https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/oakridge (to be sent), VPC diagram (will be attached), pricing example (will be attached).

Call notes: tone was cautious but engaged; primary blocker is legal sign-off and cost comparison vs self-hosting. agreed pilot approach: Dedicated pilot with strict retention and KMS.
